originality.rationale: The 2025 problem statement records only truncated prisms as a positive family, while the 2026 counterexample paper explicitly leaves truncations of simple cubic bases open. The present claim exhausts every simple cubic base through eight vertices, including non-prism types and 24-vertex truncations. Focused literature/database searches found no statement implying this cutoff. The main residual risk is inaccessible full text of the 2026 preprint; its abstract and indexed proposition-level material do not cover 24-vertex truncations of eight-vertex simple bases.
residual_risks: Direct full-text retrieval of arXiv:2607.23462 was unavailable; an unindexed remark duplicating the exact eight-base census cannot be completely excluded.

value.rationale: The 2026 counterexample leaves the simple-base truncation version open. A certified finite cutoff is mathematically motivated because it excludes all eight smallest simple cubic base types, including non-prism cases, and moves any possible counterexample to base order at least 10 and truncation order at least 30. This is a natural boundary result tied directly to the live open problem rather than an arbitrary graph slice.
